records.source: Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῆς οἰκίας ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν·
records.gloss: In the day that having gone out the Jesus from the house was sitting beside the sea;
pieces: That same day Jesus left the house and sat down beside the lake.

L.1: On that day Jesus went out of the house and was sitting beside the sea;

R.1: That same day Jesus left the house where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was staying. He went and sat down by Lake Galilee.

decisions.choice: on that day: the day of the events of chapter 12
decisions.reason: Matthew joins the parables to the conflict of chapter 12. The house is likely the one of 12:46, where his family stood outside, and Jesus goes out of it to teach the crowds.

decisions.choice: sitting beside the sea: on the shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: The Gospels call the lake a sea (4:18). Sitting was the posture of a teacher (5:1).

decisions.choice: the lake (B); Lake Galilee (R); the sea (L)
decisions.reason: As at 8:24, Balanced and Readable call it a lake, which is what it is.

decisions.choice: the house where he was staying
decisions.reason: Readable says why there was a house to leave. Matthew does not say whose house it was.

records.heading: Parables by the lake: the sower

records.source: καὶ συνήχθησαν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλοι πολλοί, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν εἱστήκει.
records.gloss: And were gathered to him crowds great, so that him into a boat having embarked to sit, and all the crowd on the shore was standing.
pieces: Such great crowds gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into a boat and sat down in it, while all the people stood on the shore.

L.2: And large crowds gathered to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into a boat and sat down, and the whole crowd was standing on the shore.

R.2: So many people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into a boat and sat down in it. All the people stood on the shore.

decisions.choice: sat in a boat: taught from a boat just off the shore
decisions.reason: A boat a little way out let the whole crowd see and hear him. Sitting was the posture of a teacher (5:1; 13:1).

decisions.choice: was standing: the crowd stood on the shore the whole time he taught
decisions.reason: The tense pictures the crowd standing as the teaching went on.

records.source: καὶ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἐν παραβολαῖς λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπείρειν.
records.gloss: And he spoke to them many things in parables saying, Behold, went out the sowing to sow.
pieces: He told them many things in parables. "Listen!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "A sower went out to sow.

L.3: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke many things to them in parables, saying, "Look, the sower went out to sow.

R.3: He taught them many things by using parables. Parables are stories that teach a lesson. Jesus said, "Listen! A farmer went out to plant seed.

decisions.choice: parables: stories and word pictures from daily life that teach about God's kingdom
decisions.reason: The word means a comparison. It covers proverbs, riddles and stories. These parables compare the kingdom of heaven to what happens on a farm, in a kitchen and at sea, and they need explaining (13:10-18, 36).

decisions.choice: the sower: a typical sower, the one in the story
alternatives: a particular man the crowd knew
decisions.reason: The article points to the figure of the story, as is usual in parables.

decisions.choice: sowing: scattering seed by hand over a field
decisions.reason: The farmer threw seed by hand as he walked, so some fell on the path and on poor ground at the edges.

decisions.choice: look (L); listen (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: Parables are stories that teach a lesson
decisions.reason: This is the first time Matthew uses the word. Readable keeps "parables" and says what they are.

decisions.choice: the sower (L); a sower (B); a farmer (R); no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Readable names a farmer, the person who did the sowing. The sower is a figure in a parable, so the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, as with the bridegroom at 9:15. Jesus later says who sows the good seed (13:37).

records.source: καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ἃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἐλθόντα τὰ πετεινὰ κατέφαγεν αὐτά.
records.gloss: And in the sowing of him some indeed fell beside the road, and having come the birds devoured them.
pieces: As he was sowing, some of the seed landed beside the path, and the birds came and ate it all up.

L.4: And as he sowed, some [seeds] fell beside the road, and the birds came and devoured them.

R.4: As he threw the seed, some of it landed on the path. Birds came and ate it.

decisions.choice: beside the road: on or along the hard path through or around the field
decisions.reason: Paths ran along and through the fields. Seed that fell there lay on hard ground, where birds found it at once.

decisions.choice: some: some seeds (the word is plural)
decisions.reason: The plural refers to seeds, which the story does not name.

decisions.choice: the path (B, R); the road (L)
decisions.reason: The word means a way or road. In a field it is a footpath.

records.source: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθέως ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς, ἡλίου δὲ ἀνατείλαντος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.
records.gloss: Others but fell upon the rocky places where not it had soil much, and immediately sprang up because of the not having depth of soil, \v 6 sun but having risen they were scorched and because of the not having root were dried up.
pieces: Some landed on rocky patches where the soil was thin. They shot up at once, since the soil was not deep,
but when the sun came up, the young plants were scorched, and having no root, they dried up.

L.5: And others fell on the rocky places, where they did not have much soil, and at once they sprang up, because they had no depth of soil;
L.6: but when the sun rose, they were scorched, and because they had no root, they withered.

R.5: Some seed landed on rocky ground, where there was not much soil. The plants came up quickly, because the soil was not deep.
R.6: But when the sun rose, the plants burned up in the heat. They dried up and died, because their roots did not go down deep.

decisions.choice: rocky places: rock with only a thin layer of soil over it
decisions.reason: Much of Galilee has limestone close under the surface. The seed warms and sprouts fast, but the roots cannot go down.

decisions.choice: others ... they were scorched: the seeds, then the plants that grow from them
decisions.reason: The Greek goes on with "they" as the seeds become plants.

decisions.choice: burned up in the heat
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the sun did.

records.source: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ ἔπνιξαν αὐτά.
records.gloss: Others but fell upon the thorns, and came up the thorns and choked them.
pieces: Other seed landed among thornbushes, and the thorns shot up and smothered it.

L.7: And others fell on the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked them.

R.7: Some seed landed where thorny weeds were growing. The weeds grew up and crowded out the young plants.

decisions.choice: thorns: thorny weeds whose roots were already in the ground
decisions.reason: The ground looked clear when the seed fell, but the thorns came up with the grain and took its light and water.

decisions.choice: crowded out the young plants
decisions.reason: Readable says how the thorns killed the grain.

records.source: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπόν, ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
records.gloss: Others but fell upon the soil the good and was giving fruit, some indeed a hundred, some but sixty, some but thirty.
pieces: But other seed landed in good soil and went on to bear grain, a hundred times as much as was sown, or sixty, or thirty.

L.8: And others fell on the good soil and were yielding fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.

R.8: But some seed landed on good soil. It grew and made a big crop. Some plants made a hundred times as much grain as was planted. Some made sixty times as much, and some made thirty times as much.

decisions.choice: a hundred, sixty, thirty: times as much as was sown
alternatives: a hundred, sixty or thirty plants
decisions.reason: The numbers count the yield. A good harvest was perhaps ten times the seed, so these are very large crops (compare Genesis 26:12, where Isaac reaps a hundredfold).

decisions.choice: fruit: grain, the crop
decisions.reason: The word is used of any crop. It prepares for the meaning given in 13:23.

decisions.choice: times as much as was sown (B); times as much grain as was planted (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the numbers count.

records.source: ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
records.gloss: The one having ears let him hear.
pieces: Whoever has ears must listen."

L.9: The one who has ears, let him hear."

R.9: If you can hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, pay attention to this!"

decisions.choice: whoever has ears, let him hear: a call to listen closely and take the saying to heart
decisions.reason: As at 11:15. The parable has a meaning the hearer must think about, as 13:10-17 shows.

decisions.choice: ears, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: ears to hear, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "ears to hear", as in Mark 4:9 and Luke 8:8. Some early manuscripts have only "ears". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: If you can hear me, pay attention to this!
alternatives: The one who has ears, let him hear
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of the saying in plain words, as at 11:15.

records.source: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖς αὐτοῖς;
records.gloss: And having come the disciples said to him, Why in parables do you speak to them?
pieces: The disciples came up to Jesus and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} using parables when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} talk to them?"

L.10: And the disciples came and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} speak to them in parables?"

R.10: Then the followers of Jesus came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They asked, "Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} use parables when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach the people?"

decisions.choice: to them: to the crowds
decisions.reason: Jesus spoke to the crowds from the boat (13:2-3). The disciples are set apart from them.

decisions.choice: came: came to him, perhaps later and away from the crowd
alternatives: while he was still in the boat
decisions.reason: Matthew does not say when they asked. Mark 4:10 says it was when Jesus was alone.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new paragraph begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: Why Jesus speaks in parables

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅτι ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἐκείνοις δὲ οὐ δέδοται.
records.gloss: He but answering said to them, Because to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, to those but not it has been given.
pieces: He answered them, "Because you have been allowed to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but they have not.

L.11: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to them, "Because to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, but to them it has not been given.

R.11: Jesus answered, "God has let you know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven. These are secrets that God is now making known. But God has not let those other people know them.

decisions.choice: mysteries: God's secrets, hidden until he makes them known
decisions.reason: In Daniel 2:28 God "reveals mysteries". The mysteries of the kingdom are what God is doing through Jesus. They are given, not worked out by cleverness (11:25-27).

decisions.choice: it has been given: God has given it
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the giver unnamed. In Jewish speech this often points to God, as in 11:25-27.

decisions.choice: because: Jesus gives the reason for speaking in parables
alternatives: introducing his words, like a colon
decisions.reason: The word can introduce quoted speech or give a reason. Here it answers the question "why".

decisions.choice: God has let you know; These are secrets that God is now making known
alternatives: it has been given to you
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the passive implies, keeps the word "mysteries" and says what it means.

records.source: ὅστις γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ περισσευθήσεται· ὅστις δὲ οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Whoever for has, it will be given to him and he will have abundance; whoever but not has, even what he has will be taken away from him.
pieces: Those who have will be given more, and they will have plenty. But those who do not have will lose even what they have.

L.12: For whoever has, it will be given to {{gender:them|him}}, and {{gender:they|he}} will have abundance; but whoever does not have, even what {{gender:they have|he has}} will be taken away from {{gender:them|him}}.

R.12: People who already have something will be given more. They will have more than enough. But people who have nothing will lose even the little they have.

decisions.choice: whoever has will be given more: those who accept what God gives will receive more understanding
alternatives: a saying about fairness in general
decisions.reason: The saying sounds like a proverb about wealth, but here it is about knowing the mysteries (13:11). The disciples have begun to understand and will be given more. Those who refuse lose even what they heard. Jesus uses the saying again in 25:29.

decisions.choice: will be given, will be taken away: God gives and takes
decisions.reason: As in 13:11, the passive points to God.

decisions.choice: those who (B); people who (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plural forms, which include men and women.

records.source: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λαλῶ, ὅτι βλέποντες οὐ βλέπουσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδὲ συνίουσιν·
records.gloss: Because of this in parables to them I speak, because seeing not they see and hearing not they hear nor understand;
pieces: So I speak to them in parables, because they look without seeing and listen without hearing or understanding.

L.13: This is why I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.

R.13: That is why I use parables when I talk to them. They look, but they do not really see. They listen, but they do not really hear or understand.

decisions.choice: because: they already do not see; the parables meet that state
alternatives: so that they will not see
decisions.reason: Mark 4:12 and Luke 8:10 say "so that", which stresses God's purpose. Matthew says "because", which stresses the hearers' own refusal. Both point to Isaiah 6:9-10, quoted next.

decisions.choice: seeing they do not see: they see the works and hear the words but miss what they mean
decisions.reason: The crowds have seen Jesus's works and heard his teaching (11:20-24; 12:22-24). They do not grasp what it shows.

decisions.choice: really see; really hear
decisions.reason: Readable adds "really" to show that the second seeing and hearing mean understanding.

records.source: καὶ ἀναπληροῦται αὐτοῖς ἡ προφητεία Ἠσαΐου ἡ λέγουσα· Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε.
records.gloss: And is fulfilled in them the prophecy of Isaiah the saying, In hearing you will hear and not not understand, and seeing you will see and not not perceive.
pieces: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is coming true: 'You will listen and listen and never understand; you will look and look and never perceive.

L.14: And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is being fulfilled, which says, 'You will hear with hearing and never understand, and you will see with seeing and never perceive.

R.14: They make the words of the prophet Isaiah come true. He said, 'You will listen and listen, but you will never understand. You will look and look, but you will never really see.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 6:9-10: God's word to Isaiah when he sent him to Israel
decisions.reason: God told Isaiah that the people would hear his message and not understand it. Matthew quotes the passage almost word for word from the Greek Old Testament. Paul uses the same words of his own hearers (Acts 28:26-27).

decisions.choice: is being fulfilled: is coming true in them now, in full
alternatives: was fulfilled once in Isaiah's day only
decisions.reason: The verb is present and has a strengthening prefix. What Isaiah's hearers did, this generation does again, and fully.

decisions.choice: you will hear with hearing, you will see with seeing: you will hear and see again and again
decisions.reason: The doubled verbs copy a Hebrew way of stressing an action.

decisions.choice: listen and listen, look and look
alternatives: hearing you will hear, seeing you will see
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the verb to show the force of the Hebrew idiom, as at Mark 4:12.

records.source: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου, καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν, καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν· μήποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.
records.gloss: Has grown fat for the heart of the people this, and with the ears heavily they heard, and the eyes of them they closed; lest they see with the eyes and with the ears hear and with the heart understand and turn, and I will heal them.
pieces: This people's heart has grown dull. Their ears barely hear, and they have shut their eyes tight. If they did not, they might see with their eyes and hear with their ears, understand with their heart and turn back, and then I would heal them.'

L.15: For the heart of this people has grown fat, and with their ears they have heard heavily, and they have closed their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn, and I will heal them.'

R.15: These people have hearts that have become hard. Their ears hardly hear, and they have shut their eyes. Otherwise their eyes might see and their ears might hear. Their minds might understand, and they might turn back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Then I would heal them.'

decisions.choice: the heart has grown fat: the mind and will have become dull and unresponsive
decisions.reason: In the Bible the heart is where people think and choose. A fat heart is one that no longer feels or responds.

decisions.choice: lest ... and I will heal them: so that they will not turn and be healed
alternatives: in the hope that they might yet turn
decisions.reason: After "lest" the last verb is future, not subjunctive. It still belongs to what the people avoid: they shut their eyes so as not to turn and be healed. Some read the future as a hint of hope.

decisions.choice: turn: turn back to God
decisions.reason: The verb is the Old Testament word for returning to God, that is, repenting.

decisions.choice: heal: restore, forgive, make whole
decisions.reason: In Isaiah, healing pictures God's forgiveness and restoration of his people (Isaiah 53:5; 57:18-19).

decisions.choice: turn back to me
decisions.reason: Readable says who they would turn to. God is speaking, so "me" takes the deity_pronoun setting, as at 12:18.

decisions.choice: grown fat (L); grown dull (B); become hard (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of fat. Balanced and Readable say what it means.

records.source: ὑμῶν δὲ μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ὅτι βλέπουσιν, καὶ τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν ὅτι ἀκούουσιν.
records.gloss: Of you but blessed the eyes because they see, and the ears of you because they hear.
pieces: But your eyes are blessed, for they see, and so are your ears, for they hear.

L.16: But blessed [are] your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.

R.16: But God has blessed you! Your eyes really see, and your ears really hear.

decisions.choice: blessed: in the happy state of those God favors
decisions.reason: As in the Beatitudes (5:3-11). The disciples are favored because God has given them to see and hear (13:11).

decisions.choice: your: stressed, in contrast with the crowds
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands first in the Greek sentence: you, unlike them.

decisions.choice: God has blessed you
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who blesses, and speaks of the disciples instead of their eyes and ears.

records.source: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ δίκαιοι ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.
records.gloss: Truly for I say to you that many prophets and righteous longed to see what you see and not saw, and to hear what you hear and not heard.
pieces: Truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see the things you now see, and never saw them; they longed to hear the things you now hear, and never heard them.

L.17: For truly I tell you that many prophets and righteous [people] longed to see what you see, and did not see [it], and to hear what you hear, and did not hear [it].

R.17: I tell you the truth, many prophets and righteous people wanted to see what you are seeing now. But they did not see it. They wanted to hear what you are hearing. But they did not hear it.

decisions.choice: prophets and righteous people: the faithful of Israel before Jesus
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls those who waited for God's promises (10:41; 23:29). They looked forward to the time of the kingdom.

decisions.choice: what you see and hear: the coming of God's kingdom in Jesus
decisions.reason: The disciples see Jesus's works and hear his words, which fulfill what the prophets hoped for (11:4-6).

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording of Jesus's solemn saying.

records.source: Ὑμεῖς οὖν ἀκούσατε τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ σπείραντος.
records.gloss: You therefore hear the parable of the having sown.
pieces: As for you, then, hear what the parable of the sower means.

L.18: You, therefore, hear the parable of the sower.

R.18: So listen, and I will explain to you the parable about the farmer.

decisions.choice: you: stressed, the disciples to whom it has been given to know
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out for emphasis, as in 13:16.

decisions.choice: hear: listen with understanding
decisions.reason: The disciples have already heard the story. Jesus now gives its meaning.

decisions.choice: hear what the parable means (B); I will explain (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the explanation follows.

records.heading: The sower explained

records.source: παντὸς ἀκούοντος τὸν λόγον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ μὴ συνιέντος, ἔρχεται ὁ πονηρὸς καὶ ἁρπάζει τὸ ἐσπαρμένον ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν σπαρείς.
records.gloss: Everyone hearing the word of the kingdom and not understanding, comes the evil one and snatches the having been sown in the heart of him; this is the beside the road having been sown.
pieces: Here is the seed sown beside the path: people who hear the message of the kingdom without understanding it. The evil one comes and carries off what was sown in their hearts.

L.19: When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand [it], the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in {{gender:their|his}} heart; this is what was sown beside the road.

R.19: Some people hear the message about God's kingdom, but they do not understand it. They are like the seed that fell on the path. The evil one, Satan, comes and takes away what was planted in their hearts.

decisions.choice: the evil one: the devil
decisions.reason: Here the form is clearly masculine: the evil one comes and snatches. In 13:39 the enemy is the devil; compare 5:37 and 6:13.

decisions.choice: the word of the kingdom: the message that God's kingdom has come near
decisions.reason: Jesus preached the gospel of the kingdom (4:17, 23). The seed is that message.

decisions.choice: this is what was sown beside the road: the hearer is compared with the seed sown there
decisions.reason: Jesus's words shift between the seed and the ground. The point is what happens to the word in each kind of hearer.

decisions.choice: the evil one, Satan
decisions.reason: Readable says who the evil one is, as 13:39 does ("the devil").

decisions.choice: the identification first: Here is the seed sown beside the path
decisions.reason: Balanced names the kind of ground first so that the long sentence is easy to follow when read aloud.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνων αὐτόν, οὐκ ἔχει δὲ ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιρός ἐστιν, γενομένης δὲ θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζεται.
records.gloss: The but upon the rocky places having been sown, this is the one the word hearing and immediately with joy receiving it, \v 21 not he has but root in himself but temporary is, having happened but tribulation or persecution because of the word immediately he is caused to stumble.
pieces: The seed sown on the rocky ground is the person who hears the word and at once accepts it with joy.
But the word has no root in them, and they hold on only for a while. As soon as hardship or persecution comes on account of the word, they stumble and fall away.

L.20: And what was sown on the rocky places, this is the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy,
L.21: but has no root in {{gender:themselves|himself}} and lasts only for a time; and when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, at once {{gender:they fall|he falls}} away.

R.20: Other people are like the rocky ground. They hear the message and right away they accept it with joy.
R.21: But they do not let it put down roots in them, so they last only a short time. Then trouble comes, or people hurt them because of the message. Right away they give up.

decisions.choice: falls away: is tripped up and stops following
decisions.reason: The verb means to trip over something. Here the trouble makes them give up the word they received.

decisions.choice: lasts only for a time: temporary, not lasting
decisions.reason: The word means "for a season". Their joy is real but does not last.

decisions.choice: trouble or persecution: hardship, and attacks from others
decisions.reason: The first word means pressure or distress, the second being hunted down for one's faith (5:10-12).

decisions.choice: give up
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for what the verb means here.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων, καὶ ἡ μέριμνα τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου συμπνίγει τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.
records.gloss: The but into the thorns having been sown, this is the one the word hearing, and the worry of the age this and the deceit of the riches choke the word, and unfruitful it becomes.
pieces: The seed sown among the thorns is the person who hears the word, but the cares of the present age and the false promises of wealth smother it, so that it yields no crop.

L.22: And what was sown among the thorns, this is the one who hears the word, and the worry of this age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

R.22: Other people are like the ground with thorny weeds. They hear the message, but then they worry about the things of this life. They are fooled into thinking that being rich will make them happy. These things crowd out the message, so it does not produce anything in their lives.

decisions.choice: the worry of this age: the anxious cares of life in the present world
alternatives: concern for the end of the world
decisions.reason: Jesus warned against such worry in 6:25-34. "This age" is the present time, before the age to come (12:32).

decisions.choice: the deceitfulness of wealth: riches that promise what they cannot give
decisions.reason: The word means deceit or seduction. Wealth draws the heart away from God (6:19-24; 19:21-24).

decisions.choice: it becomes unfruitful: the word produces no crop in that person
decisions.reason: The plant does not die at once. It grows but gives no grain.

decisions.choice: They are fooled into thinking that being rich will make them happy
decisions.reason: Readable explains how wealth deceives.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν καλὴν γῆν σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ συνιείς, ὃς δὴ καρποφορεῖ καὶ ποιεῖ ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
records.gloss: The but upon the good soil having been sown, this is the one the word hearing and understanding, who indeed bears fruit and produces, some indeed a hundred, some but sixty, some but thirty.
pieces: But the seed sown on good soil is the person who hears the word and understands it. That person does bear fruit, yielding a hundred times what was sown, or sixty, or thirty."

L.23: But what was sown on the good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands [it], who indeed bears fruit and produces, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty."

R.23: But some people are like the good soil. They hear the message and understand it. Then they produce a good crop. Some produce a hundred times as much as was planted, some sixty times as much, and some thirty times as much."

decisions.choice: hears and understands: takes in the message and grasps it
decisions.reason: Understanding is the difference between this hearer and the first (13:19). It is what the crowds lack (13:13-15).

decisions.choice: bears fruit: shows the word in a changed life
decisions.reason: Fruit in Matthew means the deeds that show what a person is (3:8; 7:16-20; 12:33).

decisions.choice: who indeed: this one, and no other, bears fruit
decisions.reason: The small word adds emphasis.

records.source: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ σπείραντι καλὸν σπέρμα ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Another parable he set before them saying, Has been likened the kingdom of the heavens to a man having sown good seed in the field of him.
pieces: Then Jesus set another parable before them: "The kingdom of heaven is like the story of a man who sowed good seed in his field.

L.24: He put another parable before them, saying, "The kingdom of the heavens has been compared to a man who sowed good seed in his field.

R.24: Then Jesus told them another parable. He said, "The kingdom of heaven is like what happened when a man planted good seed in his field.

decisions.choice: has been compared: the kingdom is like the whole story that follows
alternatives: the kingdom is like the man
decisions.reason: The verb is a past passive, "has been made like". The comparison is with what happens in the story, not with the man alone.

decisions.choice: put before: set out for them to consider
decisions.reason: The verb is used of setting food before guests and of setting out teaching.

decisions.choice: like the story of a man (B); like what happened when a man (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that the comparison is with the whole story. The man who sows is a figure in a parable, so the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, as with the bridegroom at 9:15.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: Weeds among the wheat

records.source: ἐν δὲ τῷ καθεύδειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ὁ ἐχθρὸς καὶ ἐπέσπειρεν ζιζάνια ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σίτου καὶ ἀπῆλθεν.
records.gloss: In but the sleeping the men came of him the enemy and sowed over weeds in the middle of the wheat and went away.

L.25: But while {{gender:people|men}} were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and went away.

R.25: But one night, while everyone was asleep, the man's enemy came. He planted weeds among the wheat and then left.

decisions.choice: weeds: darnel, a weedy grass that looks like wheat until it forms heads
decisions.reason: The word names a grass of grain fields whose seeds are bitter and can make people ill. While young it is hard to tell from wheat (13:26).

decisions.choice: the enemy sowed weeds: a known act of spite against a farmer
decisions.reason: Sowing weeds in someone's field was a way to ruin a harvest. Roman law later dealt with this kind of damage.

decisions.choice: while people were sleeping: at night, when no one would see
decisions.reason: The phrase sets the time. It does not blame the man's workers.

decisions.choice: weeds
decisions.reason: "Darnel" is a rare word and "tares" an old one. All levels say "weeds" and the meaning note names the plant.

decisions.choice: one night
decisions.reason: Readable says when people slept.

records.source: ὅτε δὲ ἐβλάστησεν ὁ χόρτος καὶ καρπὸν ἐποίησεν, τότε ἐφάνη καὶ τὰ ζιζάνια.
records.gloss: When but sprouted the grass and fruit produced, then appeared also the weeds.
pieces: When the wheat came up and began to form heads of grain, the weeds showed up as well.

L.26: And when the plants sprouted and produced grain, then the weeds also appeared.

R.26: The wheat grew and made heads of grain. Then everyone could see the weeds too.

decisions.choice: then the weeds appeared: only when the grain formed could the darnel be told apart
decisions.reason: The weeds were there from the start, but they looked like wheat until the heads formed.

decisions.choice: the plants: the green blades of grain
decisions.reason: The word means grass or green plants. Here it is the young wheat.

records.source: προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου εἶπον αὐτῷ· Κύριε, οὐχὶ καλὸν σπέρμα ἔσπειρας ἐν τῷ σῷ ἀγρῷ;

L.27: And the slaves of the householder came and said to him, 'Master, did you not sow good seed in your field?

R.27: The owner's servants came to him. They said, 'Master, you planted good seed in your field, did you not?

decisions.choice: slaves: servants owned by the householder
decisions.reason: The word means slaves, as at 8:9 and 10:24-25. Large households had slaves who worked the land.

decisions.choice: Master: a respectful address to the owner
alternatives: Lord, as an address to God
decisions.reason: The word means lord or master. In the story it is the slaves' address to their owner.

decisions.choice: did you not sow good seed?: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The slaves are sure the seed was good and so cannot explain the weeds.

decisions.choice: Master
decisions.reason: The slaves speak to their owner, so all levels say "Master". The householder is a figure in a parable, so the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, as with the bridegroom at 9:15.

decisions.choice: landowner (B); owner (R); householder (L)
decisions.reason: He owns the house and the field.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that they were owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: πόθεν οὖν ἔχει ζιζάνια;
records.gloss: From where then has it weeds?
pieces: So where have these weeds come from?'

L.27: Where then does it get weeds?'

R.27: So where did all these weeds come from?'

decisions.choice: where then: the slaves cannot account for the weeds
decisions.reason: "Then" draws the conclusion: if the seed was good, the weeds came from somewhere else.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς· Ἐχθρὸς ἄνθρωπος τοῦτο ἐποίησεν.
records.gloss: He but said to them, Enemy a man this did.
pieces: 'An enemy has done this,' he told them.

L.28: And he said to them, 'A man [who is] an enemy did this.'

R.28: He answered, 'Someone who hates me did this.'

decisions.choice: an enemy, a man: some enemy, a hostile person
alternatives: a man who is my enemy, named
decisions.reason: The two nouns together mean "an enemy". The owner knows it was done on purpose.

decisions.choice: Someone who hates me
decisions.reason: Readable says what an enemy is.

records.source: οἱ δὲ δοῦλοι αὐτῷ λέγουσιν· Θέλεις οὖν ἀπελθόντες συλλέξωμεν αὐτά;
records.gloss: The but slaves to him say, Do you want then having gone away we should gather them?
pieces: 'Shall we go out, then, and gather them up?' the servants asked.

L.28: And the slaves say to him, 'Do you want us, then, to go and gather them up?'

R.28: The servants asked him, 'Do you want us to go and pull up the weeds?'

decisions.choice: do you want us to gather them?: a polite request for orders
decisions.reason: The slaves are ready to act at once and ask what their owner wishes.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ὁ δέ φησιν· Οὔ, μήποτε συλλέγοντες τὰ ζιζάνια ἐκριζώσητε ἅμα αὐτοῖς τὸν σῖτον·
records.gloss: He but says, No, lest gathering the weeds you uproot together with them the wheat;
pieces: 'No,' he replied, 'for in gathering the weeds you might pull up the wheat with them.

L.29: But he says, 'No, lest while gathering the weeds you uproot the wheat along with them.

R.29: 'No,' he answered. 'When you pull up the weeds, you might pull up some of the wheat with them.

decisions.choice: uprooting the wheat: the roots of the two plants are tangled together
alternatives: the slaves cannot tell the plants apart
decisions.reason: By now the plants can be told apart (13:26), but their roots have grown together in the soil.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: ἄφετε συναυξάνεσθαι ἀμφότερα μέχρι τοῦ θερισμοῦ· καὶ ἐν καιρῷ τοῦ θερισμοῦ ἐρῶ τοῖς θερισταῖς· Συλλέξατε πρῶτον τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας πρὸς τὸ κατακαῦσαι αὐτά, τὸν δὲ σῖτον συναγάγετε εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην μου.
records.gloss: Let grow together both until the harvest; and in time of the harvest I will say to the harvesters, Gather first the weeds and bind them into bundles in order to burn them, the but wheat gather into the barn of me.
pieces: Leave them to grow side by side until the harvest. When harvest time comes, I will give the reapers their orders: "Pull out the weeds first, and tie them into bundles for burning. But store the wheat in my barn."'"

L.30: Let both grow together until the harvest; and at the time of the harvest I will say to the harvesters, "Gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn."'"

R.30: Let the wheat and the weeds grow together until harvest time. Then I will tell the workers, "First pull up the weeds and tie them together. They will be burned. Then bring the wheat into my barn."'"

decisions.choice: bundles to burn: darnel was gathered and used as fuel
decisions.reason: Wood was scarce, and dried weeds were burned in ovens. The picture also points to judgment (3:12; 13:40-42).

decisions.choice: the harvest: a picture of God's final judgment
decisions.reason: John the Baptist used the same picture of wheat gathered and chaff burned (3:12). Jesus explains it in 13:39.

decisions.choice: reapers (B); workers (R); harvesters (L)
decisions.reason: The word means those who harvest. Balanced uses the traditional word for those who cut grain; Readable a plain one.

records.source: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔσπειρεν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: Another parable he set before them saying, Like is the kingdom of the heavens to a grain of mustard, which having taken a man sowed in the field of him;
pieces: He gave them another parable to think about: "Picture a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in his field. The kingdom of heaven is like that.

L.31: He put another parable before them, saying, "The kingdom of the heavens is like a grain of mustard, which a man took and sowed in his field;

R.31: Jesus told them another parable. He said, "The kingdom of heaven is like a tiny mustard seed. A man planted it in his field.

decisions.choice: a grain of mustard: a tiny seed of a garden plant that grows several feet tall
decisions.reason: The mustard seed was known for being very small (17:20). Black mustard grew in Galilee and could reach a man's height or more.

decisions.choice: the kingdom is like: like what happens to the seed in the story
decisions.reason: As in 13:24, the comparison is with the whole story: a small beginning and a great end.

decisions.choice: the picture first, then the comparison
alternatives: the kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed
decisions.reason: Balanced draws the picture first and then applies it to the kingdom, to keep the long sentence clear when read aloud.

decisions.choice: tiny
decisions.reason: Readable says why a mustard seed was chosen, as at Luke 13:19.

records.heading: The mustard seed and the yeast

records.source: ὃ μικρότερον μέν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων, ὅταν δὲ αὐξηθῇ μεῖζον τῶν λαχάνων ἐστὶν καὶ γίνεται δένδρον, ὥστε ἐλθεῖν τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατασκηνοῦν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: which smaller indeed is of all the seeds, when but it is grown greater than the garden plants it is and becomes a tree, so that come the birds of the heaven and nest in the branches of it.
pieces: Of all the seeds it is the smallest, but once it is grown it stands taller than the other garden plants and turns into a tree, big enough for wild birds to come and nest among its branches."

L.32: which is smaller than all the seeds, but when it has grown, it is greater than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches."

R.32: It is the smallest seed that people plant. But when it grows, it is bigger than all the other plants in the garden. It becomes a tree. Birds come and make their nests in its branches."

decisions.choice: smaller than all the seeds: the smallest seed people knew to sow
alternatives: the smallest seed in the whole world
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the seeds his hearers planted, not of all plants. The mustard seed was the proverbial small thing.

decisions.choice: the birds nesting in its branches: a picture of a great kingdom that shelters many
decisions.reason: The prophets use this picture of a great kingdom (Ezekiel 17:23; 31:6; Daniel 4:12, 21). Some see the nations coming in; the parable does not say.

decisions.choice: a tree: a plant as big as a tree
decisions.reason: The mustard plant is not a tree, but it grows as large as one and has branches strong enough for birds.

decisions.choice: make their nests
decisions.reason: The verb means to settle or live in a shelter. Readable uses the simplest picture.

records.source: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς· Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ζύμῃ, ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ἐνέκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον.
records.gloss: Another parable he spoke to them, Like is the kingdom of the heavens to leaven, which having taken a woman hid in of flour measures three until was leavened all.
pieces: He told them another parable: "The kingdom of heaven is like yeast. A woman took it and worked it into {{units:about 40 pounds|three measures}} of flour, until all the dough had risen."

L.33: He spoke another parable to them: "The kingdom of the heavens is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until all [of it] was leavened."

R.33: Jesus told them another parable: "The kingdom of heaven is like yeast. A woman mixed a little yeast into a large amount of flour, {{units:about 40 pounds|three measures}}. Soon all the dough had risen."

decisions.choice: leaven: a lump of old, fermented dough kept back to make the next batch rise
decisions.reason: A little leaven works through a whole batch of dough. Elsewhere leaven pictures bad influence (16:6, 11-12); here it pictures the kingdom spreading through everything, for good.

decisions.choice: hid: mixed in, so that it could not be seen
decisions.reason: The word is unusual for mixing dough, and it fits the point: the kingdom is at work even when it is hidden (13:35, 44).

decisions.choice: three measures of flour: a very large amount, enough bread for a great many people
decisions.reason: A measure (saton) was a dry measure of perhaps 7 to 13 liters; the estimates vary. Sarah baked from three measures of flour for her three visitors (Genesis 18:6).

decisions.choice: yeast (B, R); leaven (L)
decisions.reason: "Leaven" is no longer an everyday word, as at Luke 13:21.

decisions.choice: about 40 pounds by default; "three measures" as the Measures alternative
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the unit, as at Luke 13:21. The size of a saton is uncertain, so the figure is approximate.

records.source: Ταῦτα πάντα ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν παραβολαῖς τοῖς ὄχλοις, καὶ χωρὶς παραβολῆς οὐδὲν ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς·
records.gloss: These things all spoke the Jesus in parables to the crowds, and without a parable nothing he was speaking to them;
pieces: Everything Jesus said to the crowds {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said in parables; indeed, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told them nothing at all without a parable.

L.34: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables, and without a parable {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking nothing to them,

R.34: Jesus used parables to teach all these things to the crowds. He always used parables when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them.

decisions.choice: without a parable he was speaking nothing to them: his way of teaching the crowds at this time
alternatives: he never spoke plainly to anyone
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes his practice in this setting. He explained the parables to his disciples (13:36).

decisions.choice: a positive statement: He always used parables
alternatives: without a parable he said nothing
decisions.reason: The double negative is turned into a positive statement, which says the same thing more plainly.

records.source: ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Ἀνοίξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὸ στόμα μου, ἐρεύξομαι κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ καταβολῆς.
records.gloss: so that may be fulfilled the [thing] spoken through the prophet saying, I will open in parables the mouth of me, I will utter things having been hidden from foundation.
pieces: This was so that the word spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled: "I will open {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth in parables; I will pour out what has been hidden since the world was founded."

L.35: so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, "I will open {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from [the] foundation [of the world]."

R.35: This made what the prophet had said come true: "I will speak using parables. I will tell things that have been kept secret since God made the world."

decisions.choice: Psalm 78:2: the psalmist's opening words, fulfilled in Jesus's parables
decisions.reason: Psalm 78 is a psalm of Asaph that retells Israel's history as a lesson. Its second verse promises to speak in a parable and to utter dark sayings from of old. Matthew sees the words come true in Jesus's teaching. The first line follows the Greek Old Testament; the second is closer to the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: through the prophet, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: through Isaiah the prophet, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, among them the first hand of Codex Sinaiticus, read "through Isaiah the prophet", though the words come from Psalm 78:2. Early Christian writers already knew this reading. It may be original, and copyists removed the name because it seemed a mistake; or a copyist added Isaiah, the prophet Matthew names most. The Psalms were counted as prophecy, and Asaph is called a seer in 2 Chronicles 29:30. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: from the foundation, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: from the foundation of the world, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "of the world", the usual form of the phrase (25:34). Some early manuscripts lack it. Either way the sense is the beginning of the world. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: a span on "my"
decisions.reason: The psalmist's words are fulfilled in Jesus, who speaks in parables, so the pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting, as with the servant at 12:18.

decisions.choice: [of the world] (L); since the world was founded (B); since God made the world (R)
decisions.reason: "The foundation" alone does not say what was founded. All levels supply the world, which the phrase always means.

decisions.choice: I will speak using parables
alternatives: I will open my mouth in parables
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of the idiom and so has no pronoun for the speaker except "I".

records.source: Τότε ἀφεὶς τοὺς ὄχλους ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν.
records.gloss: Then having left the crowds he went into the house.
pieces: Then Jesus sent the crowds away and went into the house.

L.36: Then, leaving the crowds, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went into the house.

R.36: Then Jesus left the crowds and went into the house.

decisions.choice: leaving: sending away, dismissing
decisions.reason: The verb has many senses, among them to let go and to forgive. Here he leaves the crowds or sends them home.

decisions.choice: the house: the house of 13:1
decisions.reason: Jesus returns to the house he left at the start of the chapter.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new scene begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.heading: The weeds explained

records.source: καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διασάφησον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν τῶν ζιζανίων τοῦ ἀγροῦ.
records.gloss: And came to him the disciples of him saying, Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field.
pieces: His disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Tell us plainly what the parable of the weeds in the field means."

L.36: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field."

R.36: His followers came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "Please explain to us the parable about the weeds in the field."

decisions.choice: explain: make clear, explain fully
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something plain.

decisions.choice: explain, the reading of the SBLGNT
