records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ὁ σπείρων τὸ καλὸν σπέρμα ἐστὶν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·
records.gloss: He but answering said, The one sowing the good seed is the Son of the Man;
pieces: He answered, "The sower of the good seed is the Son of Man.

L.37: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said, "The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man;

R.37: Jesus answered, "The man who planted the good seed is the Son of Man.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's name for himself
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the title of himself (8:20; 12:40). The title recalls Daniel 7:13-14, where one like a son of man receives a kingdom.

decisions.choice: the one who sows: the one sowing now, as he speaks
alternatives: only at the end of time
decisions.reason: The present participle fits Jesus's work of sowing the word now (13:19).

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀγρός ἐστιν ὁ κόσμος· τὸ δὲ καλὸν σπέρμα, οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας· τὰ δὲ ζιζάνιά εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ πονηροῦ, ὁ δὲ ἐχθρὸς ὁ σπείρας αὐτά ἐστιν ὁ διάβολος· ὁ δὲ θερισμὸς συντέλεια αἰῶνός ἐστιν, οἱ δὲ θερισταὶ ἄγγελοί εἰσιν.
records.gloss: the and field is the world; the and good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom; the and weeds are the sons of the evil one, \v 39 the and enemy the having sown them is the devil; the and harvest consummation of age is, the and harvesters angels are.
pieces: The field is the world. The good seed stands for the people who belong to the kingdom, and the weeds for the people who belong to the evil one.
The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.

L.38: and the field is the world; and the good seed, these are the {{gender:children|sons}} of the kingdom; and the weeds are the {{gender:children|sons}} of the evil one,
L.39: and the enemy who sowed them is the devil; and the harvest is [the] end of [the] age, and the harvesters are angels.

R.38: The field is the world. The good seed is the people who belong to God's kingdom. The weeds are the people who belong to the evil one.
R.39: The enemy who planted the weeds is the devil. The harvest is the end of the world, and the workers who gather the harvest are angels.

decisions.choice: the world: the whole world of people, where the kingdom's seed is sown
decisions.reason: The field is wider than Israel or the church. Good and evil people live side by side in it until the end.

decisions.choice: sons of the kingdom, sons of the evil one: those who belong to the kingdom, those who belong to the evil one
alternatives: the people of Israel by birth
decisions.reason: "Sons of" names those who belong to something. In 8:12 "sons of the kingdom" are those who assumed a place by birth; here they are those who truly belong to it.

decisions.choice: the end of the age: the completion of this age, when God judges
alternatives: the end of a period of history
decisions.reason: The phrase is Matthew's (13:40, 49; 24:3; 28:20). It is the close of the present age and the start of the age to come.

decisions.choice: the devil: the slanderer, the evil one of 13:19
decisions.reason: The devil tempted Jesus (4:1-11). Here he is the enemy who works against the kingdom.

decisions.choice: the people who belong to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means. Literal keeps it with the gender setting, as at 8:12.

decisions.choice: the end of the world
decisions.reason: "The age" is not plain to young readers. Readable uses a familiar phrase for the same time.

records.source: ὥσπερ οὖν συλλέγεται τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ πυρὶ καίεται, οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος·
records.gloss: Just as therefore are gathered the weeds and with fire are burned, so it will be in the consummation of the age;
pieces: The weeds are collected and burned up in the fire, and the end of the age will be like that.

L.40: Just as, then, the weeds are gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the end of the age.

R.40: The weeds are gathered and burned in the fire. That is what it will be like at the end of the world.

decisions.choice: burned with fire: a picture of God's judgment on the wicked
alternatives: the weeds are only destroyed for fuel
decisions.reason: The burning of the weeds pictures what happens to evildoers at the judgment (3:10-12; 7:19).

decisions.choice: the end of the world
decisions.reason: As in 13:39.

records.source: ἀποστελεῖ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ, καὶ συλλέξουσιν ἐκ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ σκάνδαλα καὶ τοὺς ποιοῦντας τὴν ἀνομίαν, καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
records.gloss: Will send out the Son of the Man the angels of him, and they will gather out of the kingdom of him all the causes of stumbling and those doing the lawlessness, \v 42 and they will throw them into the furnace of the fire; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth.
pieces: The Son of Man will send {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels, who will collect from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom everything that leads people into sin and everyone who breaks God's law.
They will throw them into the burning furnace, and there people will weep and grind their teeth.

L.41: The Son of Man will send out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels, and they will gather out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom all the causes of stumbling and those who practice lawlessness,
L.42: and they will throw them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

R.41: The Son of Man will send out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels. They will take out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom everything that makes people sin, and all the people who do evil.
R.42: The angels will throw them into the fire that burns like a furnace. There they will cry and grind their teeth.

decisions.choice: causes of stumbling: whatever leads people to sin, and those who cause it
decisions.reason: The word means a trap or a stone to trip over. In Matthew it is what makes people fall into sin (18:7).

decisions.choice: the causes of stumbling and those who do lawlessness: perhaps Zephaniah 1:3
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Zephaniah 1:3 God says he will sweep away the stumbling blocks along with the wicked. Jesus's words may echo it.

decisions.choice: the furnace of fire: Daniel 3:6
decisions.reason: In Daniel those who would not bow to the king's statue were to be thrown into a blazing furnace. Here the furnace pictures God's judgment.

decisions.choice: weeping and gnashing of teeth: anguish and rage
decisions.reason: As at 8:12. Matthew repeats the phrase (13:50; 22:13; 24:51; 25:30).

decisions.choice: everyone who breaks God's law (B); the people who do evil (R)
decisions.reason: Lawlessness means living as if God's law did not apply (7:23). Balanced and Readable say it in plain words.

decisions.choice: people will weep and grind their teeth (B); they will cry and grind their teeth (R)
decisions.reason: As at 8:12.

records.source: Τότε οἱ δίκαιοι ἐκλάμψουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: Then the righteous will shine out as the sun in the kingdom of the Father of them.
pieces: In their Father's kingdom, then, the righteous will blaze out like the sun.

L.43: Then the righteous will shine out like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.

R.43: Then the people who do what God wants will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.

decisions.choice: the righteous will shine like the sun: Daniel 12:3
decisions.reason: Daniel says that at the resurrection the wise will shine like the brightness of the sky. The verb has a strengthening prefix: they will shine out.

decisions.choice: the righteous: those who do God's will
decisions.reason: In Matthew the righteous are those who live as God wants (5:20; 25:37, 46). They stand in contrast to the evildoers of 13:41.

decisions.choice: the people who do what God wants
decisions.reason: Readable says what "righteous" means here.

records.source: ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.
records.gloss: The one having ears let him hear.
pieces: Whoever has ears must listen.

L.43: The one who has ears, let him hear.

R.43: If you can hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, pay attention to this!

decisions.choice: whoever has ears, let him hear: a call to listen closely and take the saying to heart
decisions.reason: As at 11:15 and 13:9. Here the call follows a warning of judgment.

decisions.choice: ears, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: ears to hear, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: As at 13:9, many manuscripts read "ears to hear". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: If you can hear me, pay attention to this!
alternatives: The one who has ears, let him hear
decisions.reason: As at 11:15 and 13:9. The speech goes on, so no quotation mark closes here.

records.source: Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν θησαυρῷ κεκρυμμένῳ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, ὃν εὑρὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔκρυψεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτοῦ ὑπάγει καὶ πωλεῖ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει καὶ ἀγοράζει τὸν ἀγρὸν ἐκεῖνον.
records.gloss: Like is the kingdom of the heavens to treasure having been hidden in the field, which having found a man hid, and from the joy of him he goes and sells all as much as he has and buys the field that.
pieces: The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure buried in a field. A man came across it and covered it up again. Then, full of joy, he went and sold everything he owned and bought that field.

L.44: The kingdom of the heavens is like treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid; and in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.

R.44: The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure that was hidden in a field. One day a man found it, and he hid it again. He was filled with joy. So he went and sold everything he owned, and he bought that field.

decisions.choice: treasure hidden in a field: valuables buried for safekeeping
alternatives: a treasure placed there for him
decisions.reason: With no banks, people buried money and jewels, especially in time of war, and some was never recovered.

decisions.choice: in his joy: his joy is the reason he sells everything
decisions.reason: "His" refers to the man. Giving up everything is not a loss to him; it comes from his joy.

decisions.choice: the point is the worth of the kingdom, not the man's conduct
decisions.reason: The parable does not judge whether he should have told the owner. It shows that the kingdom is worth everything a person has.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: a man, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The man who finds the treasure is a figure in a parable, so the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, as with the bridegroom at 9:15.

records.heading: Treasure, a pearl and a net

records.source: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ ἐμπόρῳ ζητοῦντι καλοὺς μαργαρίτας·
records.gloss: Again like is the kingdom of the heavens to a man merchant seeking fine pearls;
pieces: Or again, the kingdom of heaven is like a trader who was searching for fine pearls.

L.45: Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a merchant seeking fine pearls;

R.45: Here is another picture of the kingdom of heaven. A merchant was looking for fine pearls.

decisions.choice: a merchant seeking fine pearls: a wholesale dealer who traveled to buy
decisions.reason: The word means a trader who travels. Pearls came from the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea and were among the most valued of jewels.

decisions.choice: the kingdom is like a merchant: like what happens in his story
decisions.reason: As in 13:24, the comparison is with the story as a whole.

decisions.choice: a merchant
decisions.reason: The Greek says "a man, a merchant", a way of saying "a merchant".

records.source: εὑρὼν δὲ ἕνα πολύτιμον μαργαρίτην ἀπελθὼν πέπρακεν πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν καὶ ἠγόρασεν αὐτόν.
records.gloss: having found but one very precious pearl having gone away has sold all as much as he had and bought it.
pieces: When he came upon a single pearl of very high price, he went and sold off all his possessions and bought it.

L.46: and having found one very valuable pearl, he went away and sold all that he had and bought it.

R.46: He found one pearl that was worth a great deal. So he went and sold everything he had, and he bought that pearl.

decisions.choice: sold: the perfect tense, a decisive and complete sale
decisions.reason: The tense stresses that the sale was made and done. He kept nothing back.

decisions.choice: selling everything: the kingdom is worth more than all else
decisions.reason: The point, as in 13:44, is the surpassing worth of the kingdom (compare 19:21, 29).

records.source: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν σαγήνῃ βληθείσῃ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐκ παντὸς γένους συναγαγούσῃ·
records.gloss: Again like is the kingdom of the heavens to a dragnet having been cast into the sea and from every kind having gathered;
pieces: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a dragnet that was let down into the lake and pulled in fish of every kind.

L.47: Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a dragnet that was cast into the sea and gathered [fish] of every kind;

R.47: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a big fishing net. People put it into the lake, and it caught all kinds of fish.

decisions.choice: a dragnet: a long net with floats on top and weights below, drawn to shore
decisions.reason: Boats or men on the shore dragged it through the water, and it caught everything in its path. It is a different word from the net of 4:18.

decisions.choice: of every kind: fish of every kind, good and bad
decisions.reason: The parable speaks of fish. The application comes in 13:49.

decisions.choice: the lake (B, R); the sea (L)
decisions.reason: As at 13:1.

records.source: ἣν ὅτε ἐπληρώθη ἀναβιβάσαντες ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν καὶ καθίσαντες συνέλεξαν τὰ καλὰ εἰς ἄγγη, τὰ δὲ σαπρὰ ἔξω ἔβαλον.
records.gloss: which when it was filled having drawn up onto the shore and having sat down they gathered the good into vessels, the but bad out they threw.
pieces: When it was full, they hauled it onto the beach, sat down, and sorted the good fish into baskets, while the worthless ones they threw away.

L.48: which, when it was full, they drew up onto the shore, and sitting down, they gathered the good into containers, but threw the bad out.

R.48: When the net was full, the fishermen pulled it up on the shore. They sat down and sorted the fish. They put the good fish into baskets. But they threw away the bad fish.

decisions.choice: the bad: fish that could not be eaten or sold
decisions.reason: The word means rotten or worthless. Some fish were unclean under the law, having no fins or scales (Leviticus 11:9-12), and some were simply useless.

decisions.choice: containers: vessels or baskets for the catch
decisions.reason: The word means any container.

decisions.choice: the fishermen
decisions.reason: Readable says who drew up the net.

records.source: οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος· ἐξελεύσονται οἱ ἄγγελοι καὶ ἀφοριοῦσιν τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκ μέσου τῶν δικαίων καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
records.gloss: So it will be in the consummation of the age; will come out the angels and will separate the evil from middle of the righteous \v 50 and will throw them into the furnace of the fire; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of the teeth.
pieces: The end of the age will be like this. The angels will go out and remove the wicked from among the righteous,
and they will throw them into the burning furnace. There people will weep and grind their teeth.

L.49: So it will be at the end of the age: the angels will go out and separate the evil from among the righteous
L.50: and will throw them into the furnace of fire; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

R.49: That is how it will be at the end of the world. The angels will come and take the evil people away from the people who do what God wants.
R.50: The angels will throw the evil people into the fire that burns like a furnace. There they will cry and grind their teeth.

decisions.choice: the angels will separate the evil from the righteous: the final judgment
decisions.reason: As in 13:41-42, the separation is done by angels at the end, not by people now (13:29-30).

decisions.choice: the furnace of fire: as in 13:42 and Daniel 3:6
decisions.reason: The same words close both explanations.

decisions.choice: the people who do what God wants
decisions.reason: As in 13:43.

decisions.choice: the end of the world
decisions.reason: As in 13:39.

records.source: Συνήκατε ταῦτα πάντα;
records.gloss: Have you understood these things all?
pieces: Have you understood all this?"

L.51: Have you understood all these things?"

R.51: Do you understand all these things?"

decisions.choice: no words introduce the question, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: "Jesus says to them" before the question, in many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Jesus says to them" before the question. Without it, the question continues Jesus's speech. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: understood: grasped the meaning
decisions.reason: Understanding is what the crowds lacked (13:13-15, 19) and what the good soil has (13:23).

records.source: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ναί.
records.gloss: They say to him, Yes.
pieces: "Yes," they answered.

decisions.choice: Yes, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Yes, Lord, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Lord" to the disciples' answer. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τοῦτο πᾶς γραμματεὺς μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐκβάλλει ἐκ τοῦ θησαυροῦ αὐτοῦ καινὰ καὶ παλαιά.
records.gloss: He but said to them, Because of this every scribe having been discipled to the kingdom of the heavens like is to a man master of a house who brings out out of the treasure of him new things and old.
pieces: He told them, "That is why every scribe who has been trained as a disciple for the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who draws from his store of treasures both new things and old."

L.52: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Because of this, every scribe who has been made a disciple for the kingdom of the heavens is like a man [who is] master of a house, who brings out of his treasure new things and old."

R.52: Then Jesus said to them, "So every teacher of the law who has become a follower in the kingdom of heaven is like the owner of a house. He brings out new things and old things from the place where he keeps his treasures."

decisions.choice: made a disciple for the kingdom: taught as a disciple, for the kingdom
alternatives: made a disciple of the kingdom
made a disciple in the kingdom
decisions.reason: The verb is passive and the phrase "the kingdom" has no preposition. It can mean trained for the kingdom, or taught about it, or made its disciple. The sense is close in each case.

decisions.choice: scribe: a teacher of the law; here one who has become Jesus's disciple
decisions.reason: Scribes were experts in the law of Moses. A scribe taught by Jesus knows both the old law and what is new in the kingdom (5:17-20).

decisions.choice: new things and old: what is new in Jesus's teaching together with the old Scriptures
decisions.reason: The householder uses both. Jesus came not to abolish the law and the prophets but to fulfill them (5:17).

decisions.choice: treasure: a storeroom, a store of valuable things
decisions.reason: The word means both the treasure and the place where it is kept.

decisions.choice: scribe (L, B); teacher of the law (R)
alternatives: expert in the law at every level
decisions.reason: The settled wording. The householder is a figure in a parable, so the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, as with the bridegroom at 9:15.

records.source: καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς παραβολὰς ταύτας, μετῆρεν ἐκεῖθεν.
records.gloss: And it happened when finished the Jesus the parables these, he went away from there.
pieces: When Jesus had finished telling these parables, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moved on from there.

L.53: And it happened, when Jesus had finished these parables, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went away from there.

R.53: When Jesus finished telling these parables, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left that place.

decisions.choice: when Jesus had finished: the formula that closes the third long speech
decisions.reason: Matthew ends each great speech with these words (7:28; 11:1; 19:1; 26:1). This one closes the parables of chapter 13.

decisions.choice: went away: moved on, set out from there
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift and move on, used of a journey.

records.source: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν, ὥστε ἐκπλήσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ λέγειν· Πόθεν τούτῳ ἡ σοφία αὕτη καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις;
records.gloss: And having come into the hometown of him he was teaching them in the synagogue of them, so that to be astonished them and to say, From where to this one the wisdom this and the miracles?
pieces: Jesus came to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hometown and began teaching the people in their synagogue. They were astounded. "Where did this man get such wisdom," they asked, "and these mighty works?

L.54: And coming into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hometown, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, "Where did this [man] get this wisdom and these mighty works?

R.54: Jesus went back to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hometown, Nazareth. He taught the people in their synagogue, and they were amazed. They said, "Where did this man get such wisdom? Where did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} get the power to do these miracles?

decisions.choice: his hometown: Nazareth, where he grew up
decisions.reason: The word means one's native place. Jesus grew up in Nazareth (2:23) and now lived in Capernaum (4:13).

decisions.choice: mighty works: acts of power, miracles
decisions.reason: As at 11:20. They have heard of his works or seen some of them.

decisions.choice: where did this man get: the question doubts the source of his gifts
decisions.reason: "This one" sounds dismissive. The questions that follow show they cannot believe one of their own could have such gifts (13:57).

decisions.choice: Nazareth
decisions.reason: Readable names the town, known from 2:23.

decisions.choice: Where did @he get the power to do these miracles?
decisions.reason: Readable makes the second half of the question a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new section begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

records.source: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ τέκτονος υἱός;
records.gloss: Not this is the of the carpenter son?
pieces: This is the carpenter's son, is it not?

L.55: Is this not the carpenter's son?

R.55: This man is only the son of the carpenter!

decisions.choice: carpenter: a builder or craftsman in wood or stone
decisions.reason: The word covers anyone who builds, in wood most often but also in stone. The point is that they know his family as ordinary working people. Mark 6:3 calls Jesus himself the carpenter.

decisions.choice: is this not?: a question that expects "yes" and belittles him
decisions.reason: They know who he is and so refuse to accept what he does.

decisions.choice: a statement with "only"
alternatives: is this not the carpenter's son?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes" and is meant to belittle. Readable says it as a statement and makes the tone plain with "only".

records.source: οὐχ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ λέγεται Μαριὰμ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Σίμων καὶ Ἰούδας;
records.gloss: Not the mother of him is called Mary and the brothers of him James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
pieces: Is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother not the woman called Mary? And are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers not James, Joseph, Simon and Judas?

L.55: Is not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother called Mary, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?

R.55: We all know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, Mary. And we know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers, James, Joseph, Simon and Judas.

decisions.choice: brothers: the ordinary word for brothers in the same family
alternatives: sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage
decisions.reason: The word normally means brothers. Christian traditions differ on whether these were sons of Mary and Joseph, sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage, or close relatives such as cousins. The text names them brothers and does not settle the question (see 1:25; 12:46).

decisions.choice: Joseph, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Joses, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read Joses, as in Mark 6:3; Joses is a short form of the same name. A few read John. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: James and Judas: two of the brothers named elsewhere
alternatives: the apostles of the same names
decisions.reason: They are not the apostles James and Judas of 10:2-4. A James, the Lord's brother, later led the church in Jerusalem (Galatians 1:19; Acts 15:13), and the letter of Jude names its writer as a brother of James (Jude 1).

decisions.choice: We all know
alternatives: Is not his mother called Mary?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes". Readable says what the townspeople mean as a statement.

records.source: καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ οὐχὶ πᾶσαι πρὸς ἡμᾶς εἰσιν;
records.gloss: And the sisters of him not all with us are?
pieces: And are all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters not living here among us?

L.56: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters, are they not all with us?

R.56: All {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sisters live right here in our town too.

decisions.choice: his sisters: unnamed, but living in the town
decisions.reason: Matthew names the brothers but not the sisters. "All" shows there were at least two. They still live in Nazareth, among the people speaking.

decisions.choice: with us: living among us
decisions.reason: The point is that the family is ordinary and well known in the town.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
alternatives: are they not all with us?
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes". Readable gives the answer.

records.source: πόθεν οὖν τούτῳ ταῦτα πάντα;
records.gloss: From where then to this one these things all?
pieces: So where did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} get all this?"

L.56: Where then did this [man] get all these things?"

R.56: So where did {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} get all these things?"

decisions.choice: where then: since his family is ordinary, where could this come from?
alternatives: a real search for his teacher
decisions.reason: "Then" draws the conclusion from their questions. The question leaves open the answer that his wisdom comes from God.

records.source: καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ.
records.gloss: And they were caused to stumble in him.
pieces: And they were offended by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.57: So they turned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and would not accept {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: took offense: stumbled over him, so as to reject him
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 13:21 of falling away. They could not get past his ordinary family and so turned from him (11:6).

decisions.choice: turned against him and would not accept him
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that taking offense here means rejecting him.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: The but Jesus said to them, Not is a prophet without honor except in the hometown and in the house of him.
pieces: But Jesus told them, "Prophets are honored everywhere except in their own hometown and among their own family."

L.57: But Jesus said to them, "A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and in his household."

R.57: But Jesus said to them, "People honor a prophet everywhere except in his own town and in his own home."

decisions.choice: a saying about prophets that Jesus applies to himself
decisions.reason: The words have the form of a proverb. By using it here, Jesus counts himself a prophet rejected by his own (compare 21:11, 46).

decisions.choice: household: his own family
decisions.reason: The word means house and so the family that lives in it.

decisions.choice: his (L, R); their (B); no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The pronoun belongs to the general saying about any prophet, so it takes no span. Balanced makes the saying plural.

decisions.choice: a positive statement: honored everywhere except
decisions.reason: The double negative is turned into a positive statement, which says the same thing more plainly, as at Mark 6:4.

records.source: καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἐκεῖ δυνάμεις πολλὰς διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: And not he did there miracles many because of the unbelief of them.
pieces: Because they would not believe, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not do many mighty works there.

L.58: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

R.58: The people there did not believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did only a few miracles there.

decisions.choice: not many mighty works because of their unbelief: they did not come to him in faith
decisions.reason: Mark 6:5 says he could do no mighty work there except heal a few sick people. Matthew says he did not do many. Throughout Matthew, healing comes to those who come to Jesus in faith (8:10, 13; 9:2, 22, 29).

decisions.choice: unbelief: refusal to trust him
decisions.reason: The noun is the opposite of faith. It sums up their response in 13:54-57.

decisions.choice: they would not believe (B); did not believe in him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a verb, which is plainer than the noun.

decisions.choice: only a few miracles
decisions.reason: Readable turns the negative into a positive statement with the same meaning.
